answer: Each identity must anchor a continuous proof chain: a fresh signed attestation in every kernel window, with mirror consecutive successes unlocking the vertex of locked stake. A missed slot resets progress. Forging N identities means sustaining N parallel chains, each with its own stake and bandwidth. Marginal cost grows superlinearly because cluster detection flags high-fanout topology, forcing higher stakes per identity. Verifiers sample at O(log N) while attackers pay O(N^2) to keep all chains alive. Sybil clusters collapse economically.
